value.body: A process engineer looks after how a plant unit runs — temperatures, pressures, flows, yields and energy use — and works out how to make it safer and more efficient. Refineries, fertiliser, petrochemical, specialty-chemical and pharmaceutical plants hire them. A day mixes checking unit data, working through problems with the operations team, and planning trials or small modifications.

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Process simulators (Aspen-type), DCS data, P&IDs, Excel

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Plant-based; shift duty is common at entry

items.label: GATE CH paper (2024)
items.note: 16,930 registered; PSUs use this paper for recruitment
items.source: GATE 2024 Statistical and Performance Report (IISc Bengaluru)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as graduate engineer trainees through campus placement at process companies. Refining, gas and fertiliser PSUs typically recruit through GATE (Chemical paper) followed by interviews. Some start as shift or production engineers and move into process roles.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading P&IDs and process flow diagrams
Process safety practices (HAZOP, permits, management of change)

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is at plant sites, often in industrial clusters away from big cities.
Common next roles: senior process engineer, technical services, process design, plant or production manager.
Hands-on plant years are valued if you later move to design or consulting work.
